nodes.question: Is the book visibly positioned behind the flower, with the flower in front of it?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the flower in front of and occluding the book in a way that establishes the book is behind it. Fail if the image clearly shows the book is not behind the flower. Unknown if the relative depth or occlusion cannot be determined from the image.
nodes.binding: Assess only the book’s and flower’s relative positions and visible occlusion in the edited image.

nodes.question: In the edited image, does the book appear behind a flower, based on relative placement and any visible depth or overlap cues?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image provides clear visual evidence that the book is behind a flower; overlap or occlusion may support this, but is not the only possible depth cue. Fail if the image clearly shows the book is not behind a flower. Unknown if the relevant flower, book, or their relative depth cannot be determined. Do not treat the separate open book as the requested book.
nodes.binding: Use the source image to identify the original closed book and rose, then inspect their placement in the edited image. Assess the requested behind relationship using relative placement and visible depth cues; do not require a single rigid cue or count unrelated flower changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show any progress toward moving the book behind the flower, even if the requested placement is not complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image provides clear evidence of partial progress toward placing the book behind the flower, such as a changed relative position or partial occlusion consistent with that placement, without establishing complete fulfillment. Fail if the image clearly shows no progress toward the requested placement. Unknown if progress cannot be determined from the image.
nodes.binding: Compare the book’s and flower’s relative positions and occlusion in the edited image; do not count unrelated edits as progress.

nodes.question: Is the book visibly positioned behind the flower?
nodes.criteria: Use s1 and s3 as evidence about final placement, and s2 as evidence about source-to-edit progress. Complete only when the supports establish the requested final behind relationship. Partial only when s2 establishes genuine progress but the final relationship is not established as complete. Absent only when the supports establish no requested progress. If evidence is insufficient or conflicting, report unknown; do not infer completion or progress from unrelated edits or from a support pass alone.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
